R1.description: A Codex worker record names what a lost Controller needs, written before the tree is prepared: the operator home, the captured credential digest and `lock_inherited: false`, with the tag equal to the job id; the liveness design reads only `worker_process` and the tag, never the lifecycle lock; the block is also the predicate that marks the record as a Codex worker's, whatever the adapter's name (#263)

R2.description: `resume` never re-attaches to a Codex worker: it ends the recorded group and every process carrying the tag, judges `active`, `inactive` and `unverifiable` as the review and tester records are judged, copies the credential back, removes the copy and reconciles through the shared rows, the protocol reconciliation included (#263)

R3.description: `resume --abandon` of a Codex record follows Claude's rules row by row (active refused naming `resume`, unverifiable needing the acknowledgement, inactive marked `FAILED`) and settles the credentials (#263)

R4.description: Every interrupt is covered: a `KeyboardInterrupt` before the spawn leaves `LAUNCHED` and reconciles to `INTERRUPTED`; a Controller killed with `SIGINT` leaves no tagged process; one killed with `SIGKILL` leaves an orphan that `resume` ends, with its nested children (#263)

R5.description: Nothing real reaches the branch and the Claude worker, the tester and the reviewer are unchanged with their tests: no real launcher key, Codex worker role, setting, option, exit code or gate; the live proof is recorded and the guides and roadmap state the facts in place (#263)
